Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 18-07-2022 at about 9.15 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on a Jupiter two-wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA- 41-EL-7925 as a pillion rider, the same was ridden by its rider-cum-RC owner by name Siddesh Kumar, on Bukkapattana-Hagalavadi road, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations.

While so proceeding, at about 9.15 p.m., when they were infront of petrol bunk, Bukkapattana, Tumakuru, due to his rash and negligent riding, the said rider lost control over his scooter and dashed to a pedestrian.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sira Government Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to District Hospital, Tumakur, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as Electrician and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Sira Police have registered the case against the rider of the said two-wheeler, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and Madhu B.S vs Siddresh Kumar B.R on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159302214/
2 treatment taken by him.

The policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 18-07-2022 and he was possessing valid and effective driving licence vide D.L. No.KA4120140018713, valid from 25-11-2014 to 24-11-2034.
If this Court comes to conclusion in granting any compensation to the petitioner, the respondent No.2/insurance company itself is liable to pay.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of two-wheeler package insurance policy bide No.D058947704/07032022 in respect of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 in favour of respondent No.1 and it was valid from 08-03-2022 to 07-03-2024.

It has contended that, there was delay of 9 days in reporting the alleged accident to the police, as the alleged accident is said to have taken place on 18-07-2022 and the same is reported to the police on 29-07-2022.
The insured scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 is falsely implicated in the alleged accident, with a sole intention to help the petitioner to get illegal and wrongful gain from the respondents.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has contended that, the alleged accident, if any, was self accident by the petitioner, as he was rider of the insured Jupiter scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 at the time of alleged accident.
The petitioner had no valid driving licence and he was not authorized to ride the two-wheeler on the road.

As per the private investigation taken up by the respondent No.2 through its panel investigator, the police without proper investigation appear to have deliberately registered the alleged accident case against the respondent No.1, to help the petitioner to have illegal and wrongful gain by way of compensation.
The petitioner is not entitled to seek for any compensation from the respondents for his own negligence and self-accident.

Further it is contended that, the alleged injuries suffered by the petitioner are simple in nature, the said injuries have healed up, there is no any deformity or disability suffered by him and he is capable to discharge his routine and normal duties and activities.
The petitioner has not suffered any loss of income.

Further it is contended that,
the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

The petitioner himself was the rider of the insured two- wheeler scooter at the time of the alleged accident, he had no valid driving licence authorizing him to ride the vehicle and he was not wearing safety helmet,

. The respondent No.1/owner of the insured two-wheeler has willfully entrusted the vehicle to the petitioner, who had no valid driving licence and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the owner of the insured motorcycle or pay any compensation to the petitioner arising out of the alleged accident.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of vehicle seizure mahazar, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 is discharge summary, Ex.P.9 is OPD record, Ex.P.10 are medical reports, Ex.P.11 is x-ray, Ex.P.12 medical bills (total 11), Ex.P.13 are prescriptions, Ex.P.14 is notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.15 is in-patient record, Ex.P.16 is OPD record, Ex.P.17 is x-ray, Ex.P.18 is referral out form, Ex.P.19 is licence issued by Department of Electrical Inspectorate and Ex.P.20 are marks cards (total 4).

12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925.
Due to rash and negligent riding, the rider of said scooter has lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the pedestrian on the said road and fell down along with his scooter.
Due to said impact, the petitioner who was pillion rider on the said scooter also fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his face, right leg and other parts of the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

No doubt, as per the Ex.R.2 investigation report of R.W.1, at the time of accident the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle bearing No. KA-41-EL-7925 and he has dashed the pedestrian and caused the accident and later, in order to claim compensation, the petitioner is allegedly shown as pillion rider on the said vehicle and the accused has been falsely implanted as rider of offending motorcycle, in connivance with the owner of said vehicle and the Police authorities.

sentences.text: Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

16. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of 12 feet wide Bukkapattana-Hagalavadi road, infront of Petrol Bunk,
Bukkapattana, Tumakuru.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident is not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no other vehicle involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false or concocted documents.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
17. No doubt, there is a delay of 11 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint, in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing treatment to his son, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.text: Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."

18. There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.1 First Information Report and Ex.P.2 first information statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case,

19. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary,
Ex.P.9 OPD record, Ex.P.10 medical reports, Ex.P.11 x-ray, Ex.P.15 in- patient record, Ex.P.16 OPD record, Ex.P.17 x-ray and Ex.P.18 referral out form, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner has suffered diffuse edema involving middle third of the face, tenderness of palpation bilateral zygomatic complex region, occlusion stable, segmental mobility, sutured lacerated wound upper labium and lefort 4 fracture.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that,
the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-41-EL-7925 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

20. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non- pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.14.
As per Ex.P.14, the date of birth of the petitioner is 03-07-1989.
The accident has taken place on 18-07-2022 at about 9:15 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 33 years.

the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,02,378/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,02,378/- (Rupees three lakh two thousand three hundred and seventy eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
Entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
